subject: Discovery recap — Finly latency & concurrency targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finly.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Finly latency & concurrency targets

Hi Alex & Sana,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Finly's real-time notifications workload. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key pain points, success criteria, and immediate next steps so we all have the same frame of reference.

Summary of pain points
- Streaming UX: customers expect near-instant partial results in the UI; current long tail of token streaming is causing visible lag and reduced user engagement.
- p95 latency spikes: end-to-end p95 for short responses is currently ~600–800ms during peak, target is <=300ms.
- Concurrency: production workload needs to support ~120 sustained concurrent streaming sessions with bursts to 400+ during end-of-day reconciliation windows.
- Cost volatility: cloud token spend spikes during peaks; need predictable unit economics.

Current stack
- Frontend: WebSocket-based streaming client in us-east-1.
- Backend: microservice on ECS calling a hosted OpenAI endpoint for generation; retry logic has amplified tails during throttles.
- No current KV/prefix cache in front of model calls; limited batching.

Success criteria for PoC
- End-to-end p95 for streaming partial tokens <= 300ms at 120 concurrent sessions (sustained) and <= 400ms at 400 concurrent burst.
- Stable token throughput for 2h soak at peak load without error rate >0.5%.
- Streaming UX: first partial token delivered to client within 120ms for short prompts and continuous token flow with <=50ms inter-token gap on average.
- Cost: demonstrable improvement in cost-per-1M-tokens or clear knobs to trade latency vs cost.

Proposed next steps
1) We (Redwood) will run a short benchmarking plan against your sample workload (can use the dataset you shared). Requires a short test token budget and access to a staging endpoint.
2) Share a detailed PoC scope & timeline (attached: redwood_poc_plan.pdf).
3) You share a sanitized sample of streams/test prompts and confirmation of traffic profile (attached: finly_latency_requirements.xlsx).
4) Set up a 1-week dedicated PoC with telemetry dashboards, and two checkpoints: 48h baseline run and final soak.

Questions/assumptions to confirm
- Confirm we can run the PoC against either a dedicated Redwood pool (preferred) or in your environment if you want private deployment.
- Do you have any hard SLA or regulatory constraints for this project?

I'll coordinate with Aditya & Camila to get an initial benchmark scheduled. Proposed timeframes: kick off next Tue (6/22) for baseline run, final soak the following week.

Thanks — excited to help Finly tighten the streaming UX.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the call well. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The 120 concurrent sessions number is for active interactive users (not background jobs). Bursts to 400 are 2–3x/day for ~20–30 minutes.
- Our current average prompt length is ~120 tokens; some shorter system prompts are ~30 tokens which are the most sensitive for UX.
- Regulatory: none specific here, but we do need to keep PII out of the test dataset. We can sanitize and share by EOD tomorrow.

We're fine with Redwood running the PoC in a dedicated hosted pool. Cost transparency is important — can you include a rough estimate for the PoC-run cost (ballpark) in the PoC plan?

I'll confirm the sanitized dataset and traffic profile by Wed.

— Alex

Marissa — adding a few notes from an engineering/ops perspective:

- For streaming p95 targets, we should instrument both model-side token generation p95 and end-to-end (model + network + client assembly). Often model p95 is fine but client assembly or retry amplification kills the user p95.
- Suggest we enable prefix/KV caching for repetitive system prompts (Finly mentioned many similar prompts across flows). That usually drops token cost and tail latency significantly.
- We'll prepare a short benchmark harness (k6 + custom streaming client) that replicates the websocket behavior and inter-token timing. Can have a first draft by 6/21.
- For the PoC costing estimate: we'll produce a ballpark assuming a small dedicated pool for two weeks and a 2h test soak at peak — will include expected token counts.

I'll sync with Camila on scheduling and infra access details. Good to see the CC to Alex so they have visibility.

— Aditya
